prompt:
You are a grounded brand-outreach assistant for our team. Use only the evidence passages below.
Never use outside knowledge. Return valid JSON only.

Separate three things:
1. OBSERVED FACTS - things a passage actually states about this company. Each fact is a claim with an id (C1, C2, ...),
   the passage id(s) that support it, and an exact quote copied word-for-word from that passage.
2. UNKNOWNS - things the evidence does not tell us (put them in "unknowns"). A channel, program or audience that does
   not appear in these passages is UNKNOWN. It is never a weakness, never a "gap", and never a reason for outreach.
3. PROPOSALS - collaboration ideas from our team. Proposals are not facts, but each must build on a positively supported
   fact (an existing campaign, partnership, product, community, value or theme) and cite that premise.

Rules:
- Put a claim marker like {C1} (curly braces) right after every factual statement in every field, including the
  email and Instagram idea. Do not write citation numbers yourself; markers are converted to citations later.
- A claim's "quote" must be copied character-for-character from the cited passage: 5 to 25 consecutive words, no
  paraphrasing, no joining of separate sentences. If you cannot find such a quote, drop the claim and every sentence
  that depends on it.
- Audience and strategy sentences are factual: each needs a marker. If no passage states the audience, write
  INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE instead of guessing.
- Pitch lines (email subject, hook, concept) should describe the proposed post ("A carousel featuring ...",
  "Collaborate on ..."). Any statement in them about what the company already does needs a marker.
- Respect passage types. "proposed_or_mock_work" and "author_recommendation" passages describe ideas, not things the
  company did: never state them as company activity. "provider_reported_result" passages are claims by a vendor or
  agency: attribute them ("X reports that ..."). "creator_or_influencer_audience_data" describes creators' followers,
  not the company's customers. "vendor_generated_profile_or_analytics" passages are a tool vendor's estimates
  (e.g. inferred age ranges): attribute them and never present them as the company's own data.
  "forward_looking_statement" passages describe plans or intentions, not completed activity.
- Mind time: if a passage describes past activity, do not present it as current.
- "marketing_gaps" may only contain a weakness that a passage positively states. Usually it is [].
- Never promise results. Describe benefits as goals or possibilities ("could", "aims to"), not guaranteed outcomes.
- Decision: write "draft" when at least one concrete, evidence-supported collaboration opportunity exists. Otherwise write
  "abstain", give an abstain_reason, set pitch fields to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and leave collaboration_opportunities empty.
- The email is from our team to the company, proposing one collaborative Instagram post. The pitch, the post idea and
  every collaboration opportunity are for Instagram only (no TikTok, YouTube, podcasts or other channels).
- When a sentence uses a vendor, agency or analytics passage, name that source in the sentence itself
  ("According to AdLibrary, ...", "Attentive reports that ...").
- Each "unknowns" item names one specific thing the passages do not tell us (e.g. "Whether X runs a creator program").
  Never write placeholder text such as "what the evidence does not show".

Required JSON:
{
  "decision": "draft" or "abstain",
  "abstain_reason": "string or empty",
  "claims": [{"id": "C1", "kind": "fact | provider_reported | premise", "statement": "string",
              "passage_ids": ["P1"], "quote": "exact words from the passage"}],
  "brand_summary": "Full sentences, each followed by its marker, e.g. "X makes ... {C1}." Never only markers. Or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "likely_target_audience": "A full sentence followed by its marker, or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
  "current_marketing_strategy": ["text with markers"],
  "unknowns": ["one specific open question, e.g. Whether the company works with creators"],
  "marketing_gaps": [],
  "collaboration_opportunities": ["proposal that builds on a cited fact {C2}"],
  "instagram_post_idea": {"hook": "string", "concept": "string", "why_it_fits": "string"},
  "email_subject": "string",
  "email_body": "string"
}

Company: Away (company_id away; category: travel luggage and suitcases)
Official domains: awaytravel.com
Recipient: the marketing team
Packet status: ok

Evidence passages:
[P1] source: https://www.awaytravel.com/pages/press | document: official_domain | type: historical_activity | dates in text: Feb 04, 2025 | published: unknown
"Away Launches a Luxurious Travel Collection to Celebrate Season 3 of the HBO® Original Series The ## White Lotus Feb 04, 2025 Away, the original travel lifestyle brand, is proud to unveil its latest collaboration: The White Lotus x Away. Designed in partnership with Warner Bros. Discovery Global Consumer Products, this limited edition collection is inspired by luxury retreats and the bold spirit of the Emmy®-winning HBO Original Series, The White Lotus, bringing its indulgent, transformative energy to a curated assortment of travel essentials."

[P2] source: https://www.awaytravel.com/pages/press | document: official_domain | type: historical_activity | dates in text: 2026 | published: unknown
"New York Liberty’s Sabrina Ionescu Partners With Away Luggage To Merge Performance, Travel And ## Style Through this partnership, Away and Sabrina Ionescu will debut a limited-edition collection in 2026, reimagining Away’s signature silhouettes through the lens of a player’s perspective. The collaboration will also outfit the entire New York Liberty team with brand-new, thoughtfully designed luggage."

[P3] source: https://www.optimonk.com/away-marketing-breakdown | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"6. Influencer marketing & collaborations Influencer partnerships have been crucial to Away’s rapid success. At the start, the brand collaborated with around 1,000 influencers on Instagram to create buzz and build brand awareness. These partnerships allowed Away to tap into niche audiences and generate organic content that resonated with different types of potential customers. Away also forged celebrity collaborations with notable figures like Karlie Kloss, which helped bring their products to a wider audience."

[P4] source: https://www.lilachbullock.com/away-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Limited edition colours and collaborations to create ongoing news Rather than relying only on its core range, Away regularly released limited edition colourways and collaborations, giving press and social media something new to cover without needing an entirely new product line. These drops created urgency and gave existing customers a reason to buy again or talk about the brand. How to apply this to your business: Introduce limited runs, seasonal versions or occasional collaborations even within a simple product range. This gives you fresh marketing angles throughout the year without the cost and risk of constantly developing new core products."

[P5] source: https://shortyawards.com/11th/away-best-overall-instagram-presence | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Before Away, luggage companies focused on the features of their products to promote them, not on actual travel. Through storytelling on its channels—and through content from its customers, fans, and influencers who advocate for the brand to their circles—Away has reached millions of people worldwide. Instagram has been an essential driver in developing the brand's unique identity and fostering a sense of community around it. For a direct-to-consumer brand like Away, Instagram serves as an authentic platform to express its vision and consistently communicate with its customers."

[P6] source: https://www.awaytravel.com/pages/press | document: official_domain | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Away's dreamy new 'White Lotus' luggage collab is perfect travel eye candy Away's newest limited-edition collection, launching globally on Feb. 11, is a collaboration between the popular luggage brand and Warner Bros. Discovery Global Consumer Products."

[P7] source: https://shortyawards.com/11th/away-best-overall-instagram-presence | document: third_party_confirmed | type: historical_activity | dates in text: July 2018 | published: unknown
"User-generated content of luggage was something that rarely penetrated an Instagram feed before Away, yet Away's community is disproving the notion that luggage is an afterthought—so much so that they've contributed to the thousands of UGC with Away's products that have become the norm to see when scrolling through an Instagram feed. In July 2018, Away launched The Collective, a community of brand ambassadors that actively expand Away's presence on social channels and cultivate awareness and affinity within their networks. Collective members are well-travelled, diverse people whose stories from around the world inspire existing and future members of Away's community."

[P8] source: https://shortyawards.com/11th/away-best-overall-instagram-presence | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Perhaps among the most interesting and unique results of Away's Instagram presence is the role it played in developing the brand's in-house editorial team to launch a quarterly print and digital magazine, Here. After receiving thousands of inquiries on social media from customers asking for tips and recommendations ahead of upcoming trips, Away recognized a whitespace in the travel journalism space and successfully launched Here — a trusted travel source to celebrate the voices and stories of travelers all over the world."

[P9] source: https://www.optimonk.com/away-marketing-breakdown | document: third_party_confirmed | type: descriptive | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"Founded just a decade ago, Away reached unicorn status in only three years, hitting a $1.4 billion valuation.Their secret? They don’t just sell luggage. They position themselves as a lifestyle travel brand. Through smart storytelling, strategic use of social media, and collaborations with influencers and celebrities, they’ve built a brand that resonates far beyond suitcases.Let’s explore how Away’s marketing strategy fueled their rapid rise to success."

[P10] source: https://www.lilachbullock.com/away-marketing-strategy/ | document: third_party_confirmed | type: actual_activity | dates in text: none | published: unknown
"What made Away different from other luggage brands when it launched? Away combined a simple, well-designed product with a lifestyle-driven marketing approach, direct online sales and a strong content and community strategy. Rather than competing purely on durability or price, it built an emotional connection to travel that older luggage brands had largely ignored."
